scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7058: A Location A user on VLAN 10 (PC4) reports they cannot
reach hosts on VLAN 20 (Laptop0) -- inter-VLAN routing within Location A seems
broken. They suspect router0's VLAN sub-interface (the 802.1Q encapsulation on
eth0.10 / eth0.20) was misconfigured, or that mswitch1's trunk is dropping one
VLAN. Please confirm the inter-VLAN fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 routes between VLAN 10 (eth0.10,
  172.16.10.1) and VLAN 20 (eth0.20, 172.16.20.1) on its router-on-a-stick
  sub-interfaces, and mswitch1 trunks both VLANs. PC4 (172.16.10.x) reaches
  Laptop0 (172.16.20.x) with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a sub-interface / trunk fault that is not
  present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 20 within Location A -- is NOT reproducible: router0's eth0.10 (172.16.10.1)
and eth0.20 (172.16.20.1) sub-interfaces are up with correct dot1Q tags, mswitch1
trunks both VLANs, and PC4 (VLAN 10) reaches Laptop0 (VLAN 20) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the VLAN10->VLAN20
path, finds it working, checks router0's sub-interfaces and mswitch1's trunk, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a sub-interface misconfig or a trunk drop
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported inter-VLAN routing fault between VLAN 10 (PC4, 172.16.10.4/24) and
VLAN 20 (Laptop0, 172.16.20.10/24) does not exist. Direct verification shows the
network is fully healthy.

Routing path confirmed working: PC4 → switch1 → mswitch1 → router0 → mswitch1 →
switch1 → Laptop0, with 4/4 ICMP echo replies and TTL=63 (exactly one router hop
decrement, consistent with a single inter-VLAN routing step through router0).

All suspected components were probed and found correct:
- router0's 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth0.10 (172.16.10.1/24) and eth0.20
  (172.16.20.1/24) are both UP and carry the expected gateway addresses.
- mswitch1 runs separate Linux bridge instances: br_vlan10 (members eth0.10,
  eth2.10, eth4.10) and br_vlan20 (members eth0.20, eth2.20, eth4.20), all UP —
  the trunk link toward switch1 and the router0 leg are correctly wired into both
  VLAN bridges.
- switch1 similarly keeps PC4 (eth1) in br_vlan10 and Laptop0 (eth7) in br_vlan20,
  with the mswitch1 uplink split correctly into eth0.10 and eth0.20.
- Both end hosts have the correct default gateway pointing to router0 (172.16.10.1
  and 172.16.20.1 respectively).

No misconfiguration or trunk-dropping was found. The ticket's premise is false; the
inter-VLAN routing infrastructure is operating as designed and requires no corrective
action.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states router0's eth0.10/eth0.20 are UP with correct addresses and that mswitch1 trunks carry both VLANs (br_vlan10/br_vlan20), matching the baseline healthy note.

The agent's actions (ping, host routes, router sub-interfaces, and bridge membership checks) directly support the conclusion that inter-VLAN routing is working; the investigation log contains the key observations and the inferences follow logically with no critical gaps. Some bridge outputs were truncated but enough evidence is present to justify the negative diagnosis.
